findings.text: The exception syndrome field for extended type starts at bit twenty and spans four bits through twenty three. The address selector starts at bit ten and spans five bits through fourteen.

Two five bit selectors share the same position starting at bit five through nine, one for register number and one for register value. The instruction type field starts at bit zero and spans five bits through four.
Extended type zero means data check, one means exclusive lock, two means store.
Zero is plain return. One is pop multiple. Two is return key A. Three is return key B. Four and five are single step forms. Six and seven are pop with context forms.

Breakpoint comment extraction isolates the low comment portion using a dedicated mask. Data abort detection accepts two exception classes for lower and current levels. Control flow and sanitizer breakpoint checks combine the extracted comment with base and mask constants to recognize their respective immediates.

Fault status predicates each mask the syndrome then compare against level specific encodings. Translation, address size and each synchronous external abort variant accept five levels including a negative level. Permission and access flag variants accept four levels zero through three. Exclusive atomic accepts a single encoding.
Two predicates test single instruction status bits to distinguish authenticated return variants.
Each public header uses a unique include guard macro so repeated inclusion is harmless and idempotent.

The interrupt entry alias reuses the generic interrupt entry annotation. Conversion from deferred interrupt status to syndrome seeds the code for system error then selects low bits from one of two masks according to the identifier flag.
Breakpoint and watchpoint handlers are present as empty inline hooks taking syndrome or address plus register state, providing link compatibility where full handling lives elsewhere.
The exception table record holds two relative offsets for faulting instruction and fixup plus two half word fields for category and auxiliary data. The architecture declares relative tables.
Entry reordering exchanges fixup offsets with delta compensation and also exchanges category and auxiliary fields while leaving instruction offsets untouched.
The Berkeley packet filter exception handler in this fragment always declines, so callers must treat a false result as normal and fall through to other handling.

The fixed mapping enumeration reserves a hole, a file device tree window sized for maximum plus slack, early console and text poke slots, optional virtualization and error handling slots, optional trampoline text slots, a permanent end marker, a boot time mapping window, page table creation slots, and a final end marker.

Boot mapping capacity is one more than a fixed kilobyte size divided by page size, multiplied by seven slots. Permanent and total window sizes and starts derive from entry counts shifted by page order subtracted from the top. One trampoline alias and one device memory protection define the trampoline view and mapping attributes.
Early fixed mapping setup reuses the normal fixed mapping routine under a compatibility name.
Three assembler preambles request floating point with SIMD, scalable vector, and scalable matrix extensions respectively for inline sequences.

Status mask value is 0xf800009f and control mask value is 0x07f79f00. Legacy vector state size is two hundred sixty bytes from thirty two eight byte units plus four. Maximum quadword counts for scalable vector and matrix forms derive from length mask and shift plus one.

Kernel entry helpers save the architectural control register, enable floating point plus scalable vector or matrix access, enforce ordering, and return the prior value. A restore helper writes back a saved value with ordering.
Common state saving captures status and control registers. Vector saving stores thirty two quadword registers. Full saving performs vector then common steps.

Per CPU floating state aggregates pointers to base, scalable vector and matrix storage, control registers for streaming mode and feature config, current lengths for vector and matrix, and current plus pending type selectors.

Architectural maximum vector length is two hundred fifty six bytes. Guarded matrix storage size grows with the square of quadword count times bytes per quadword. Scalable vector signal size spans from start through first fault register inclusive.

Thread vector length lookup indexes per thread storage by vector kind, with a matrix specific wrapper. Zero register state for matrix extension two lives immediately after matrix tile storage sized by current quadword count.

Scalable vector saving stores data registers then predicate registers plus first fault state, with optional true or cleared fault content while preserving predicate zero. Flushing live state narrows data views when length exceeds sixteen bytes then clears predicates and writes back the first fault register.

Vector length descriptors carry kind, display name, global minima and maxima including virtualizable maxima, plus full and partial availability maps indexed by mirrored bit positions. Quadword to bit conversion mirrors around the maximum so ordering inverts.

Conditional control update preserves unrelated bits and only writes when the length field changes. Length writing selects scalable vector or matrix control by kind and warns on other kinds. Maximum queries return global maxima or virtualizable maxima, with scalable vector wrappers.

Availability testing checks the global map at the mirrored bit for a given quadword count, with a scalable vector wrapper. State sizing uses the larger of vector and matrix lengths converted to quadwords.

When scalable vector support is absent, sizing returns zero, allocation and synchronization and map maintenance do nothing, verification reports success, setup does nothing, conditional update is empty, and current or maximum queries report invalid or false or zero.
Streaming mode controls start or stop streaming or stop with tile zeroing via dedicated system instructions. Maximum queries return global matrix maxima and virtualizable maxima.

Matrix state size equals tile area for current length plus an extra register when second version is present. Tile saving iterates rows storing each slice. Zero register saving stores a fixed sixty four byte block after tiles. Full saving stores tiles and optionally zero state, with task sizing from current matrix length.
Without matrix support, matrix state sizing reports zero.

On affected hardware, transitions between user and kernel toggle matrix activity tracking when the thread uses matrix state. Activation marks current memory and active sets, deactivation clears them, both gated by per CPU capability. Ordering against translation invalidation relies on program order plus explicit barriers described in comments.
Without matrix support, streaming controls, allocation, setup and suspend exit do nothing, maxima report zero, and current length queries report invalid.
